title: SDK dependency hygiene: progressive dep bumps, adaptive shims, and perf-guard rails
creator: Nina Patel
description: Objective: Perform coordinated, low-risk dependency upgrades across Python, JS, and Go SDKs, remove a few legacy API parameters, and introduce lightweight adaptive shims and runtime guards to avoid regressions in production. Background: Over the last 12 months we accumulated minor and transitive dependency drift across language clients which has caused intermittent CI flakes, larger bundle sizes for the JS client, and a couple of ABI-sensitive breakages in Go. This ticket scopes an audit -> bump -> verify -> rollout plan that minimizes customer impact and documents migration paths. The work touches: bundlers (esbuild/rollup), cryptography libs, http clients, and telemetry/metrics SDKs. Key constraints: keep runtime ABI stable for semver-minor bumps, preserve existing public surface for one release cycle while deprecating legacy fields, and enforce perf SLOs (cold-start and p50/p99 token latency).
acceptance_criteria: Audit report listing all direct and top-2 transitive deps per client with risk classification (low/medium/high)
Upgrade PRs for Python, JS, and Go with passing cross-language compatibility test-suite and CI flakes reduced < 1/week
Introduced adaptive shims layer that can opt-in per-client via feature flag and a migration guide for deprecated API fields
Benchmarks: JS bundle size reduced or unchanged after upgrade; cold-start median reduced or within 5%%; p99 generation latency not increased by >5%%
Rollout runbook and rollback plan validated in staging, with canary metrics defined and alerting configured
tasks: Inventory dependencies for python/js/go clients and tag semver ranges
Create compatibility harness that runs canonical end-to-end calls across language bindings
Implement adaptive shims in each client to accept legacy params and map to new surface (feature-flagged)
Bump dependencies incrementally and open single-change PRs per package per client
Run microbenchmarks (start-up, bundle size, per-token latency) pre/post bump
Publish migration guide and deprecation note; update CHANGELOGs
Canary rollout: stage -> small customer cohort -> wider rollout -> GA
Monitor canary metrics for 48h; rollback if errors or SLO regressions exceed threshold

notes: Trade-offs: larger dependency jumps increase risk of regressions but reduce long-term maintenance and security exposure. Adaptive shims add short-term complexity but enable a safer rollback path. If security review delays >5 days we will temporarily freeze Python cryptography bump and proceed with JS/Go canaries. Rollback path: revert PRs and toggle feature flags to re-enable legacy behavior.
